subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw warn, fail, or stay runtime-only when configured primary, fallback, or per-agent model refs are absent from the trusted model catalog?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the right behavior depends on maintainer intent for custom providers, forward-compatible model names, and whether catalog absence should be advisory or fail-closed.

options.title: Advisory catalog warnings
options.body: Add warnings in `config validate` and doctor for catalog-missing configured model refs, keeping custom and forward-compatible refs non-fatal.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject catalog-missing configured refs during validation or config writes, accepting the compatibility risk for custom and future provider ids.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep accepting arbitrary configured refs and rely on improved runtime errors plus fallback notices instead of adding preflight validation.

recommendation.title: Advisory catalog warnings
recommendation.body: Add warnings in `config validate` and doctor for catalog-missing configured model refs, keeping custom and forward-compatible refs non-fatal.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source provenance for the relevant validation and runtime paths points to Peter Steinberger, and the remaining blocker is product policy around config/provider behavior.
